about: Dated facts about the AI tools a team uses, sorted by the job each one does. Every fact carries its source and the date it was checked. The authoring guide is README.md beside this file; site/pages/tools.py renders /tools/ and the manuals from it.

jobs.line: Draft, reason and research, with sources

facts.fact: Cowork, the separate agent mode for multi-step knowledge work, is being folded into ordinary chat: you describe the outcome and Claude picks the tools.
Since 16 September 2026 the agent features of Cowork have been rolling into ordinary chats, starting with the Pro and Max plans.
A long task runs in Anthropic's cloud, labelled beta, and reaches your computer through the desktop app only when it needs local files, the browser or computer use.
In the merged chat the GitHub integration and conversation branching are missing for now, and incognito chats fall back to the old experience.
Research runs many searches that build on each other, across the web and your connected sources, and returns a cited report in minutes.
Claude writes and runs code in a private sandbox to make real files: Excel, PowerPoint, Word, PDF and charts.
On Team and Enterprise an owner chooses what the sandbox may reach, and the help page says network access starts off, though for Team it also says it starts at package managers only.
The help page itself warns that a hidden instruction in a file or page could make Claude run untrusted code or send data out.
A project is a self-contained workspace with its own chats and knowledge base, where you upload documents and set the project's own instructions.
Project instructions tailor Claude's replies within the project, for example a more formal tone or the view of a particular role.
On Team and Enterprise a project can be shared with view or edit permission, and the members it is shared with see its knowledge and instructions.
Even in a shared project, each member's chats stay private unless that member shares one, which creates a link to it.
On paid plans, when a project's knowledge nears the context limit, Claude switches to retrieval and the project can hold far more.
Claude Code's projects, a public beta, run related tasks as parallel cloud sessions, while projects in chat and Cowork are the earlier experience and keep working until the redesign reaches them.
Claude saves short topics about you and your work as you chat, and you can read, edit and delete each one in Settings.
Memory is on by default on individual plans; on Team and Enterprise it stays off until an owner allows it and each member turns it on.
If an owner switches memory off for the organisation, every member's memories are deleted at once.
Incognito chats stay out of history and memory, but on Team and Enterprise they are still kept for a period and appear in an owner's data exports.
A skill is a folder of instructions, scripts and resources that Claude loads only when it judges the skill relevant to the task.
Skills need code execution switched on, and a skill can run code and install packages.
The help centre says owners on Team and Enterprise can give a skill to everyone in the organisation.
Anthropic's platform docs say custom skills in the apps are per user and cannot be managed centrally.
A connector lets Claude reach another service, either one from the directory, such as Slack, Google Drive or Linear, or a custom one that points at a remote MCP server.
A custom connector is called from Anthropic's cloud, so its server must be reachable from the public internet, and one behind a VPN will not connect.
On Team and Enterprise an owner enables a connector, each member signs in, and the owner can limit read, write and delete actions for everyone.
A connector inherits each person's own permissions in the service it reaches, except a custom connector on a shared credential, which reaches whatever that credential can.
The help centre warns that custom connectors reach servers Anthropic has not verified, and advises connecting only to servers from trusted organisations.
A scheduled task is a saved prompt that Claude runs hourly, daily, weekly, on weekdays or on demand, in the cloud, so your computer can be off.
When you set up a scheduled task by hand, you choose its approval mode, along with its prompt and how often it runs.
A scheduled task works with your connectors and the files in your Claude account, and one that needs local files or apps runs only locally.
The Console's Workbench is now the playground, which keeps your current draft in your browser and has no saved prompts or prompt versions.
Claude Code is a coding agent that reads a codebase, edits files, runs commands and uses git.
The same engine runs in the terminal, VS Code, JetBrains, the desktop app, the web and the phone, and repository settings carry across the local ones.
With an API key or a cloud provider such as Amazon Bedrock you lose cloud sessions, routines, Remote Control and the Chrome integration, and on Bedrock the built-in web search too.
CLAUDE.md is a plain file of instructions loaded at the start of every session, at organisation, user, project or local scope.
CLAUDE.md is context, not enforcement: it arrives as a message after the system prompt, and the docs advise keeping each file under 200 lines.
If a repository has AGENTS.md and no CLAUDE.md, Claude Code reads AGENTS.md.
The command `/doctor prompt-audit` finds stale or conflicting instructions.
In plan mode Claude Code researches and proposes, and edits stay blocked until you approve the plan, except in a terminal session where bypass permissions are available.
Auto mode, in which a classifier model reviews actions in your place, is now the starting mode in the terminal and VS Code.
The docs say auto mode cuts prompts but does not guarantee safety, and an owner can switch it off with `disableAutoMode`.
Allow, ask and deny rules sit on top of the mode, and deny rules hold in every mode.
Hooks are your own commands that Claude Code runs at fixed points, and a hook that runs before a tool call can block it.
The sandbox limits which files and hosts shell commands can reach, and it does not cover file tools, MCP servers or hooks.
The command `/rewind` restores code, conversation or both from a snapshot taken at each prompt, but changes made by shell commands are not tracked, and it is not version control.
A subagent has its own context window, system prompt and tools, is defined as a markdown file in `.claude/agents/`, and returns a summary.
A subagent other than a fork does not see your conversation or the files Claude has read, and starts from the brief Claude writes, its own prompt and your CLAUDE.md files.
Every skill's description costs context in every session, and a skill stays in context once it is loaded.
The command `/code-review` runs a review in a background subagent of your session and follows CLAUDE.md.
At low and medium effort `/code-review` reports only the findings it is most confident in, and at high and above it may include findings it is less sure about.
The command `claude -p "prompt"` runs once and exits, and `--bare` skips hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers, memory and CLAUDE.md so every machine behaves the same.
Without `--bare`, a `-p` run executes the repository's hooks and connects its MCP servers with no trust prompt.
The command `claude --worktree name` gives a session its own checkout and branch, and ignored files such as `.env` are missing unless listed in `.worktreeinclude`.
A cloud session runs on an isolated machine and keeps going after you close the laptop: start one with `claude --cloud "task"` and pull it back with `claude --teleport`.
The cloud machine clones your GitHub remote, so commits you have not pushed are not there.
Auto-fix can answer review comments under your GitHub name, which can set off automation that is driven by comments, such as Terraform runs.
Remote Control lets you drive a session running on your own machine from claude.ai/code or the phone, as long as the local process stays alive.
Routines run a saved task in the cloud on a schedule, from an HTTP call or from a GitHub event, and act as you on GitHub and in your connectors.
A green run status means the session ran, not that the task succeeded.
Claude in Chrome is a browser extension that reads pages, clicks, types, fills forms and moves between tabs, and its Chrome side panel is in beta.
From Claude Code you start it with `claude --chrome`, and keeping it on by default adds its tool definitions to every session.
It acts directly on websites on your behalf, and the help page says plainly that, despite its safety classifiers, it is still risky.
Deep research plans, reads many sources and writes a report with citations, and you can review and edit its plan before it starts.
A project keeps related chats, files and instructions together so every chat in it starts with the same context, and a shared project uses project-only memory.
OpenAI's prompt engineering guide says to use the Playground to develop and iterate on prompts.
OpenAI's Codex CLI runs Codex in a repository from your terminal, where it inspects code, edits files and runs commands.
Codex Cloud runs coding tasks on OpenAI-managed machines, each in its own workspace, and keeps going while your computer sleeps.
Work, which replaced agent mode, browses with a cloud browser or the desktop app's own, and signs in to sites through a form the model cannot read.
ChatGPT runs a prompt once, on a schedule, or when a new Gmail message, a Slack message or GitHub pull request activity arrives.
With the Gemini API's Google Search tool the model runs the searches itself and answers with citations that link each span of text to its source.
NotebookLM was renamed Gemini Notebook on 16 July 2026, and each notebook is getting a secure cloud computer that runs code for analysis grounded in your sources.
AI Studio's playground takes a system instruction and a chat with a chosen model, with run settings at the side and a Get code button.
Google Antigravity comes as a desktop app, Antigravity 2.0, a command line tool and an IDE, and in the desktop app agents work within a project's folders and repositories.
Jules is an experimental coding agent that works on a GitHub repository in a virtual machine while you move on, and shows a plan for you to approve before it changes code.
Antigravity 2.0 is a desktop app for managing agents that can interact with Chrome and create artifacts and implementation plans.
In Antigravity 2.0 the command `/schedule` runs an instruction once at a set time or on a recurring schedule, as a scheduled task.
Cursor describes itself as a coding agent that helps you understand your codebase, plan and build features, fix bugs and review changes.
Copilot cloud agent researches a repository, plans and makes changes on a branch in its own short-lived GitHub Actions environment, and you create the pull request when you are ready.
Kiro turns a feature into a spec of requirements.md, design.md and tasks.md, then runs the tasks and shows the status of each.
Spec Kit is GitHub's open source toolkit that gives AI coding agents a set process: a constitution once per project, then specify, plan, tasks, implement and converge for each feature.
